data.name: Wizard.Help.StepRoi
data.value:
ROI (Region of Interest): • A rectangular sub-area of the camera frame — where the ML model runs. • Full frame = analyse everything. 95% of cases. • Why narrow ROI: only part of camera view is relevant (e.g. hall floor, not ceiling). Saves CPU/GPU.
Who defines ROIs: IT admin / technician in Advanced → ROI. You pick from existing or use "Full frame" for a quick start.

data.name: Wizard.Help.StepZone
data.value:
Zone (alert polygon): • A polygon inside the ROI — alerts fire only when detection falls inside. • "Whole ROI" = simplest option, polygon covers the entire rectangle. • Custom polygon: narrow strip near a gate, around a specific machine, excluding footpath.
Why zones matter: • Not every detection = alert. "Person" on public sidewalk (inside ROI but outside zone) = ignored. • "Person" inside zone "Machine area" = immediate alert.
You can add more zones later in Advanced → Zones.

data.name: Wizard.Help.Step1
data.value:
Who adds cameras: • New cameras (RTSP URL, credentials, vendor, network) are added by your IT admin / technician in Advanced → Cameras. • As a safety/BHP operator you only pick from the existing list and configure what to detect.
Tips: • If no cameras show up — request setup from IT. Provide: camera brand, location, RTSP address. • Click a card to select. Name + location should match what your IT provided.

data.name: Wizard.Help.Step2
data.value:
14 built-in safety classes (PPE, fire, traffic, safety). Click cards to pick. Class = "what to detect".
Tips: • Pick 2-5 classes at start. Easier to tune FP rates later. • For YOLO-World classes (Text) you need to compile a prompt pack before first inference (Advanced → Prompt packs). • Class has "recommended min confidence" — wizard uses this value. Tighten later in /admin/triggers if too many false alarms.
Common pitfalls: • Picking 10+ classes at once makes FP analysis hard. Start small, then grow.

data.name: Wizard.Help.Step3
data.value:
Currently: scope = full camera frame.
Why zones matter: • Not all detections = alert. You may want "person" ignored on public sidewalk, but "person in machine area" = immediate alert. • Zones can be drawn as polygons (/zones page, advanced).
For starter wizard: full frame is enough. Refine later in /zones.

data.name: Wizard.Help.Step4
data.value:
Action = what happens after a rule fires.
Recommendations: • Start with "In-app notification" — operator sees popup, zero config. Verify rules work first. • Email — add SMTP in /admin/settings. Recipient can be a group (bhp@firma.pl). • Webhook — Slack/Teams/ERP. POST JSON with payload: trigger, camera, time, detections.
Each trigger is rate-limited to 10 fires/minute by default (change in /admin/actions).

data.name: Wizard.Help.Step5
data.value:
After "Create and run": • Camera + zone + rules saved to DB. • Pipeline starts analysing frames within ~5 seconds. • You are redirected to /flow — graph of what was created.
What next: • Open /monitor to see live detections. • Open /incidents when alerts fire. • Refine thresholds in /admin/triggers (advanced).
